title: Longest Consecutive Sequence
oneLinerQuestion: Find the length of the longest sequence of consecutive numbers in an unsorted array.
explanation:
Problem Intuition: The Longest Consecutive Sequence problem requires finding the length of the longest consecutive elements sequence in an unsorted array in O(N) time. While sorting the array allows easy identification of consecutive runs, it inherently takes O(N log N) time. To achieve linear time complexity, we insert all numbers into a Hash Set to provide O(1) membership lookups. A naive search starting at every number would result in redundant traversals of sequences. Crucially, a number can only represent the start of a consecutive streak if 'num - 1' is not present in the set. Checking this condition ensures that each sequence is traced only once from its true starting point.

- Step 1: Base Case & Hash Set Population — If nums is empty, we immediately return 0. Otherwise, we insert all elements of nums into a Hash Set 'numSet' (e.g., `new Set(nums)`), removing duplicates and enabling O(1) lookup operations.

- Step 2: Global Maximum Initialization — We initialize a tracker 'longestStreak = 0' to record the maximum sequence length identified.

- Step 3: Candidate Traversal & Sequence Start Filter — We iterate through each unique number 'num' in 'numSet'. Before attempting to count a streak, we check if `!numSet.has(num - 1)`. If 'num - 1' exists, 'num' is part of an ongoing chain and will be handled when its lowest element is processed, so we skip it.

- Step 4: Forward Counting Loop — When a true sequence start is found (where `!numSet.has(num - 1)` is true), we set 'currentNum = num' and 'currentStreak = 1'. We then enter a while loop that runs as long as `numSet.has(currentNum + 1)`, incrementing 'currentNum++' and 'currentStreak++' on each iteration.

- Step 5: Global Record Update — Once the inner while loop finishes counting the contiguous chain, we update our maximum: `longestStreak = Math.max(longestStreak, currentStreak)`.

- Step 6: Termination & Return — After iterating through all numbers in the set, every contiguous sequence has been traversed from its origin. We return 'longestStreak'.

- Complexity & Memory Guarantees — Time Complexity: O(N) where N is the number of elements in nums, because each number is entered into the while loop at most once (only when it is part of a streak explored from its head). Space Complexity: O(N) auxiliary space required to store the numbers in the Hash Set.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION longestConsecutive(nums):
    numSet = SET(nums), longest = 0
    FOR num IN numSet DO:
        IF (num - 1) NOT IN numSet THEN:
            length = 1
            WHILE (num + length) IN numSet DO length = length + 1
            longest = MAX(longest, length)
        END IF
    END FOR
    RETURN longest
END FUNCTION
